A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INT/IMA framework and studies. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison after matching material across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments with 260 simulated clients, 200 human participants, a 30-person follow-up study, and downstream fine-tuning evaluations in Tables 2–4 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including human evaluations, component analyses, and the ESConv/NTConv downstream comparison.

M1.justification: Stage planning, reflection-level planning, top-5 exemplar retrieval, response generation, and IMA remain unchanged. Section 3.2.3 renames the existing retrieval input a state-augmented query without changing its components; the appendix prompts also remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ESConv-derived simulated clients, human narrative-therapy interactions, and ESConv/NTConv emotional-support tasks. No dataset, population, language, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same seven role-playing LLM baselines, with the same INT ablations in Table 3. Table 4 retains the comparison between ESConv-trained and NTConv-trained Qwen3-8B models.

E3.justification: Section 4.1.3 changes the reported number of human-rating dimensions from five to four. This corrects the description to match the four-dimension questionnaire and results already present in v1; it does not establish that the study changed or was rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablations, 30-person within-subject analysis, dialogue statistics, therapeutic-state distributions, and illustrative IM trajectory are retained. Figures 4–5 contain the same underlying graphics and observations.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 removes the dialogue-length standard deviation, SD=5.7, while retaining the mean of 32.4 rounds. Other statistical reporting, including demographic variability and annotator agreement, remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The limited numerical-result removal is the dialogue-length SD=5.7 in Appendix C.2. All scores and comparison entries in Tables 2–4, and the plotted results in Figures 4–5, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The planning-space definitions, IM categories, and Equations 1–5 retain the same mathematical content. Reflection-level index corrections standardize notation without changing definitions or reasoning; no proofs or theoretical results are added.

C1.justification: The central claims about structured narrative-therapy simulation, IM-based assessment, superiority over role-playing baselines, and support-dialogue synthesis remain the same. The expanded conclusion restates contributions already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Expanded wording about agency, self-advocacy, and broader applications restates the existing empowerment and social-use interpretations. The substantive limitations concerning culture, therapeutic timing, GPT-4o dependence, and unverified long-term well-being outcomes are unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 5 attributes the stated training steps and time to NTConv/ESConv models rather than INT, clarifying the existing setup. It removes the 28-layer and 4,608-token specifications. Appendix B also removes the explicit promise to release the full expert-response collection, although the general code/data release footnote remains.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. Section 2 elaborates the existing contrast between progression-aware narrative therapy and prior approaches, without adding cited work or substantively revising the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and terminology edits, corrects typographical errors and an author's name order, expands the conclusion, and adds acknowledgments. Limitations and Ethics become unnumbered; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5's caption explicitly identifies the horizontal axis. Table 5 becomes shorter, and appendix material is repaginated: Table 17 moves from the questionnaire page to a page shared with Table 18. The figures and main result-table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 improves internal consistency by correcting the human-rating dimension count and clarifying which models were fine-tuned. However, it removes model specifications, dialogue-length variability, and the explicit full-exemplar release promise. These clarity gains coexist with reduced reproducibility and reporting detail, while the scientific evidence remains unchanged; a reliable net improvement or deterioration is not established.
